fulltext: IT之家 9 月 17 日消息，据央视财经 9 月 16 日报道，记者从中国电力企业联合会获悉，今年以来，以互联网数据、充换电服务业为代表的数字能源新型负荷迎来爆发式增长，全国互联网数据服务业用电量超过 600 亿千瓦时，与去年同期相比增长超过四成，远超 2024 年全年水平。
报道提到，随着新质生产力加快壮大，人工智能等新兴产业成为支撑全社会用电量稳健增长最确定的力量。人工智能产业的飞速扩张，直接带动数据中心用电需求快速上涨。当前全国日均 Token 调用量较两年前实现千倍级增长，算力需求水涨船高。
截至 2026 年 7 月底，全国智能算力总规模达 245 万 PFLOPS，八大国家算力枢纽、三个算电协同发展区已建成智算规模占全国比重超 85%。
IT之家注：Token（词元）是计算机科学与自然语言处理领域中的一个基础且重要的概念，通常指文本数据经过分词或标记化处理后的最小单位，其中单位可以是单词、标点符号、数字或其他任何有意义的符号。无论是用户输入的查询请求，还是系统生成的程序代码，均需拆解为词元进行运算处理。因此，词元调用量不仅反映模型的使用活跃度，更是评估人工智能产业实际价值创造能力的重要指标。

In a lengthy essay published over the weekend, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei made a proposal that the AI industry would have rejected instantly even a year ago: embed third-party evaluators inside all frontier AI companies, giving them the power to report safety incidents, assess whether AI models are truly aligned, and share their unvarnished findings with the world.

Amodei said Anthropic would commit to giving independent evaluators like METR and Redwood Research unprecedented access to the company’s systems. CEO Sam Altman said OpenAI also would commit to the practice, signaling a potentially profound change in how the industry works with outside research groups.

Third-party evaluators who spoke to TechCrunch broadly welcomed the proposal, but said details need to be ironed out — and ideally backed by legislation — if they’re to know whether they will function as truly independent watchdogs or vendors operating on the AI companies’ terms.

That deeper access is becoming more important as models get better at recognizing when they’re being evaluated, raising the risk that they’ll behave well during testing while concealing problematic behavior. Researchers say clues to that behavior can be missed when testing the finished model, but uncovered by investigating how it behaved throughout training.

“AI companies should be able to answer some very basic questions about their training process, such as: Did the AI ever actively try to undermine its own alignment training while it was going through the training?” Alexander Meinke, head of research at Apollo Research, told TechCrunch. “The answer to this should be an unequivocal no, and right now we are completely relying on AI companies to both carefully check this themselves and then truthfully report this to the public. And we’ve seen from recent incidents that, by default, they will do neither. As embedded evaluators, we could actually check.”

Historically, AI companies brought in outside reviewers to test finished models shortly before their release. Now, evaluators that TechCrunch spoke to propose giving them access not just to the final model, but to intermediate versions, or “checkpoints,” from its lifetime of training. Adam Gleave, CEO of FAR.AI, said evaluators could compare those checkpoints to determine when concerning behavior emerged, inspect the post-training environment that rewards models for certain behaviors, and check evaluation transcripts and logs to verify a company’s claims about how a model performed.

Whether and when Anthropic and OpenAI plan to provide that kind of access is unclear. Neither company has shared which evaluators they’ll work with, when they will be embedded, how many they’ll bring on, exactly what systems and information they will be able to access or what can be disclosed to the public, despite repeated questions from TechCrunch.

Looking under the hood like this matters because models that perform well on safety tests aren’t necessarily safe if they’ve learned specifically how to pass that test. John Steidley, head of strategy at Palisade Research, pointed to an example of a “shutdown resistance benchmark” that measures if the AI will resist being shut down in certain circumstances.

“It’s extremely relevant if the AI has been trained specifically to perform well on that benchmark,” Steidley said, comparing it to Volkswagen’s Dieselgate scandal, in which cars were programmed to recognize emissions tests and perform differently under testing conditions.

Gleave noted that meaningful access could extend beyond the models themselves, with evaluators being given access to interview employees to check whether a company’s documentation and public descriptions of its safety practices match what happened internally.

Amodei did outline a fairly comprehensive proposal that might give evaluators the kind of access they think is necessary, including the right to “publish key findings about risk levels, incidents, practices, and the access they received or didn’t receive — without editorial control by Anthropic.”

But evaluators say such a system will only work if AI companies are actually willing to surrender control over the process. Previous efforts at independent evaluations suggest that that surrender will be hard won, as third parties have often run up against tensions over access, time, confidentiality, and what they can say publicly.

Gleave said FAR.AI has had to turn down contracts with several frontier developers that wanted too much control over the evaluation process, threatening the firm’s independence. By default, he said evaluators are treated like ordinary contractors: bound by restrictive NDAs and agreements that give developers significant control over what can ultimately be published.

There’s also the question of whether reviewers will get enough time and access to do the work they’re being asked to do. When investigating the Hugging Face incident, OpenAI gave METR and Redwood roughly a week on premises to investigate, and both later said they could not draw confident conclusions due, in part, to scope and timing limitations.

A similar issue occurred during the pre-release testing for GPT-6 Astra, which OpenAI has touted as its most aligned model yet. According to Apollo Research’s contribution to the model card, the firm was given only three days to test Astra, which made it difficult to draw firm conclusions.

“Apollo believes that, given the higher rates of eval awareness and limited evaluation window, low rates of misbehavior here do not provide substantial evidence about the model’s alignment or misalignment,” the firm wrote in its evaluation.
That track record leaves evaluators with a basic question: Why should this time be different?

“It’s certainly possible that Dario and Sam just had a change of heart, and they’re going to be very open about this,” Gleave said. “But the intellectual property of these companies is so incredibly valuable to them, and I think they’re going to, by default, be very careful about what can be shared.”

Several researchers who spoke to TechCrunch called for a transparent framework that they all agree to publicly. Part of the framework, says Steidley, should involve standards for what kinds of auditors companies can rely on, lest they try to sidestep the issue by shopping for evaluators that either aren’t qualified or aren’t interested in assessing the most concerning risk.
Henry Papadatos, executive director of Safer AI, says the problem, even with a public framework, is that voluntary measures are always dependent on a company’s goodwill.

“Ideally, we would have good regulation mandating this…because then companies cannot change their mind tomorrow if they have a big PR crisis,” Papadatos told TechCrunch, noting that it’s also a good means of pushing all companies to adhere to the rules, not only the most willing.

Not everyone has signed on. So far, Meta, SpaceXAI, and Google DeepMind have not committed to embedding third-party evaluators, though DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis has proposed a separate industry standards body to independently test frontier models. Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic have also privately been discussing AI safety plans for weeks.

Some laws are already forming around the idea of third-party evaluators. California’s SB 53, signed into law last year, requires large frontier AI developers to publish safety frameworks and report critical safety incidents. A new law, SB 813, signed this month, creates a framework for state-recognized “independent verification organizations” with expertise assessing AI risks.

In Europe, the EU AI Act requires frontier developers to conduct and document model evaluations and adversarial testing and report serious incidents. The EU AI Office can also conduct its own evaluations and appoint independent experts.

For now the law remains less expansive than what Amodei is proposing, leaving frontier labs largely responsible for deciding how much independent scrutiny they will submit to. Papadatos said voluntary self-regulation is better than nothing, but ultimately, companies can’t demand the freedom to control their own safety rules while also asking the public to trust that they’re following them.
“You cannot have it both ways, having zero accountability externally, and then say, ‘I’ll just have my own flexible rules,” Papadatos said.

在周末发表的一篇长文中， Anthropic首席执行官Dario Amodei提出了一项建议，即即使在一年前，人工智能行业也会立即拒绝：将第三方评估人员嵌入所有前沿人工智能公司，让他们有权报告安全事件，评估人工智能模型是否真正一致，并与世界分享他们毫不掩饰的发现。
Amodei表示， Anthropic将致力于为METR和Redwood Research等独立评估人员提供前所未有的公司系统访问权限。首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼(Sam Altman)表示， OpenAI也将致力于这一做法，这标志着该行业与外部研究团体的合作方式可能发生深刻变化。
接受TechCrunch采访的第三方评估人员广泛欢迎这项提议，但表示，如果想知道他们是否将作为真正的独立监督机构或按照人工智能公司的条款运营的供应商，就需要解决细节问题，最好是立法支持。
随着模型更好地识别何时进行评估，这种更深入的访问变得越来越重要，这增加了它们在测试期间表现良好的风险，同时隐藏了有问题的行为。研究人员表示，在测试完成的模型时，这种行为的线索可能会被遗漏，但通过调查它在整个训练过程中的表现来发现。

“人工智能公司应该能够回答有关其培训过程的一些非常基本的问题，例如：人工智能在进行培训时是否曾积极尝试破坏自己的定位培训？”阿波罗研究院研究主管亚历山大·梅恩克（ Alexander Meinke ）告诉TechCrunch。“对此的答案应该是明确的'不' ，现在我们完全依赖人工智能公司自己仔细检查，然后向公众如实报告。我们从最近的事件中看到，默认情况下，他们不会这样做。作为嵌入式评估人员，我们实际上可以进行检查。”
从历史上看，人工智能公司在发布之前不久就引入了外部审核人员来测试已完成的模型。现在， TechCrunch采访的评估人员建议让他们不仅可以访问最终模型，还可以访问中间版本或“检查点”。FAR.AI首席执行官Adam Gleave表示，评估人员可以比较这些检查点，以确定何时出现相关行为，检查奖励模型某些行为的培训后环境，并检查评估成绩单和日志，以验证公司关于模型表现的说法。
Anthropic和OpenAI是否以及何时计划提供这种访问权限尚不清楚。尽管TechCrunch一再提出问题，但两家公司都没有透露他们将与哪些评估人员合作，何时嵌入，将带来多少评估人员，他们将能够访问哪些系统和信息，或者可以向公众披露哪些信息。
像这样看待引擎盖很重要，因为在安全测试中表现良好的模型，如果他们已经学会了如何通过该测试，就不一定是安全的。Palisade Research战略主管约翰·斯泰德利（ John Steidley ）指出了一个“关机阻力基准”的例子，该基准可以衡量人工智能在某些情况下是否会抵制关机。
Steidley说： “如果人工智能经过专门训练，能够在该基准上表现出色，那么这一点就极为重要。”他将其与大众汽车的柴油门丑闻进行了比较，该丑闻中，汽车被编程为识别排放测试，并在测试条件下表现不同。
Gleave指出，有意义的访问可以扩展到模型本身之外，评估人员可以访问面试员工，以检查公司的文件和其安全实践的公开描述是否与内部发生的情况相匹配。
Amodei确实概述了一项相当全面的提案，可能会使评估人员获得他们认为必要的访问权限，包括有权“发布有关风险水平、事件、实践以及他们收到或没有收到的访问权限的关键调查结果—无需Anthropic的编辑控制”。
但评估人员表示，只有人工智能公司真正愿意放弃对这一过程的控制，这样的系统才能发挥作用。以前在独立评估方面的努力表明，这种投降是来之不易的，因为第三方经常在访问、时间、保密性以及他们可以公开表达的内容方面遇到紧张局势。
Gleave表示， FAR.AI不得不拒绝与几家希望过多控制评估过程的前沿开发商签订合同，威胁到公司的独立性。他表示，默认情况下，评估人员被视为普通承包商：受限制性NDA和协议的约束，这些协议赋予开发商对最终可以发布的内容的重要控制权。
还有一个问题是，审稿人是否有足够的时间和访问权限来完成他们被要求做的工作。在调查拥抱脸事件时， OpenAI给了METR和Redwood大约一周的时间进行调查，后来他们都表示，由于范围和时间限制，他们无法得出自信的结论。
在GPT-6 Astra的发布前测试期间也发生了类似的问题， OpenAI将其吹捧为迄今为止最一致的型号。根据Apollo Research对模型卡的贡献，该公司只给了三天的时间来测试Astra ，这使得很难得出确切的结论。
该公司在评估中写道： “Apollo认为，鉴于评估意识较高且评估窗口有限，这里的不当行为率较低并不能提供有关模型对齐或不对齐的实质性证据。”
这一记录给评估者留下了一个基本问题：为什么这次应该有所不同？
Gleave说： “Dario和Sam肯定会改变主意，他们会对此非常开放。” “但这些公司的知识产权对他们来说非常有价值，我认为，默认情况下，他们会对可以共享的内容非常小心。”
几位接受TechCrunch采访的研究人员呼吁建立一个透明的框架，他们都公开表示同意。Steidley说，框架的一部分应该包括公司可以依赖哪种审计师的标准，以免他们试图通过寻找不合格或对评估最令人担忧的风险不感兴趣的评估人员来回避问题。
Safer AI执行董事Henry Papadatos表示，即使有公共框架，问题在于自愿措施总是取决于公司的善意。
帕帕达托斯告诉TechCrunch ： “理想情况下，我们会有良好的监管来强制要求这样做……因为如果明天公司面临严重的公关危机，他们就不能改变主意。”他指出，这也是推动所有公司遵守规则的好方法，而不仅仅是最愿意遵守规则的公司。
并非所有人都已登录。到目前为止， Meta、SpaceXAI和Google DeepMind还没有承诺嵌入第三方评估人员，尽管DeepMind首席执行官Demis Hassabis已经提出了一个单独的行业标准机构来独立测试前沿模型。几周来，谷歌、OpenAI和Anthropic也一直在私下讨论人工智能安全计划。
一些法律已经围绕第三方评估人员的想法形成。去年签署成为法律的加利福尼亚州SB 53要求大型前沿人工智能开发人员发布安全框架并报告关键安全事件。本月签署的一项新法律SB 813为国家认可的“独立核查组织”创建了一个框架，这些组织具有评估AI风险的专业知识。
在欧洲，《欧盟人工智能法案》要求前沿开发人员进行模型评估和对抗性测试，并报告严重事件。欧盟人工智能办公室也可以进行自己的评估并任命独立专家。
目前，该法律仍然没有Amodei提议的那么广泛，让前沿实验室在很大程度上负责决定他们将接受多少独立审查。Papadatos表示，自愿自我监管总比没有好，但最终，公司不能要求自由控制自己的安全规则，同时还要求公众相信他们正在遵守这些规则。
Papadatos说： “你不能两者兼而有之，对外不负任何责任，然后说， ‘我只是有我自己的灵活规则。”

cards.title: The 2.5-hour AI-generated Odyssey movie is 2.5 hours too long
cards.title_cn: 这部2.5小时的人工智能电影《奥德赛》太长了2.5小时
cards.summary: 【The Verge】Christopher Nolan's engrossing take on The Odyssey dominated at the box office and spurred a newfound interest in classic literature among filmgoers. But a new retelling of the story made entirely wit…
fulltext: Going up against Christopher Nolan with AI slop was ill-advised.

Christopher Nolan’s engrossing take on The Odyssey dominated at the box office and spurred a newfound interest in classic literature among filmgoers. But a new retelling of the story made entirely with AI is so bad that it might just make viewers hate the original tale altogether.

The new film, called Odysseus: The Fall, comes via AI firm Fountain 0 and is written and directed by company cofounder Ash Koosha, who also lent his likeness to the title character and created all of the music. (The film’s credits are very short.) The studio’s only previous work is an AI film called Dreams of Violets that made it into Tribeca earlier this year. The Fall is, on its face, a much more ambitious project, billed as “the first completely AI generated film produced at the level of a Hollywood blockbuster.” In reality, it’s nothing close to “the level of a Hollywood blockbuster.” That may not necessarily be surprising, but after watching the entire 2.5-hour production I nonetheless found myself constantly surprised by just how much worse things could get. The Fall is the opposite of a glimpse at the future of AI filmmaking — it’ll make you wonder if there’s really any future in it at all.

The movie is available to rent now for $9.99 and, as far as I can tell, you can only watch it via a web browser. In order to view it on my living room TV I had to mirror the screen from my phone, which is not exactly IMAX in 70mm. Things didn’t get much better once I pressed play.

The Fall is plagued by two main issues. The first is consistency. The world of the film is constantly morphing, to the point that it’s incredibly distracting. The height of the cyclops that traps Odysseus and his men changes from shot to shot, waves move in the opposite direction of the wind, mouths don’t match the words spoken (and sometimes they move without producing a sound at all), and oars bend and twist as sailors row. In one scene a huge fleet of boats is racing through the ocean and one of them is inexplicably moving sideways. The AI-produced voice-overs can be incomprehensible, and at various points the names of both Odysseus and Zeus are pronounced wrong.

If it were just the odd hiccup it might be understandable, but there are so many faults in The Fall that it can be hard to focus on anything else. I watched the movie with my 13-year-old kid and it basically became a game of finding the weirdest mistakes. I noticed that a sword magically turned into a dagger, and then she one-upped me by spotting an alien carcass roasting over a spit. The Fall seems like a film designed to prove why script supervisors exist.

The thing is, while all of the AI-induced errors are distracting, they’re also the most entertaining part of the movie. There isn’t really much to distract from in The Fall because it is so dull. Because current AI models are really only capable of generating scenes that last a few seconds, the movie feels like a disjointed collection of moments from the odyssey that have been stitched together with little rhyme or reason. If you didn’t already know the story going into this, I don’t think you’d have any idea of what was going on, because the film explains very little. You don’t even learn about Penelope’s suitors until the movie is almost over.

I also can’t think of a single aspect of The Fall that feels improved because of AI. The “acting” is bafflingly bad, with characters pausing for seconds at a time for no apparent reason and bursts of laughter that jolt you out of nowhere. There’s no weight to the action, as if this takes place in a world where things like physics and gravity are suggestions rather than constants. Similarly, there aren’t any cool or impressive effects that wouldn’t be possible without the technology. The monsters look like shabby stop-motion creatures from the 1930s, which is all the weirder when they’re put beside the smooth, hyperreal human characters that AI spews out. It’s not just jarring, it’s boring and ugly.

Koosha claims that he adapted this story because he “always felt passionately about Homer’s epic tale since [he] originally read it years ago.” It seems much more likely that he’s trying to skate by on the hype and energy created by Nolan’s film, turning AI slop into a modern-day iteration of direct-to-video cash grabs. But this also puts the film at an incredible disadvantage from the very beginning, inviting comparisons to one of the most critically and commercially successful movies of the last few years, one that was especially beloved because of the director’s insistence on human craftsmanship. Nolan is someone who cares deeply about film, and his passion and enthusiasm is why stars want to work with him and viewers flock the theaters to see his movies.

The existence of The Fall, meanwhile, shows utter contempt for the medium, attempting to boil the work of hundreds of skilled workers into slop produced by a tiny team. It’s so terrible it’ll make you appreciate human-made art all the more.

cards.summary_cn: 【The Verge】克里斯托弗·诺兰（ Christopher Nolan ）对《奥德赛》（ The Odyssey ）的引人入胜的看法在票房上占据主导地位，并激发了电影观众对经典文学的新兴趣。但这个故事的新复述完全是机智的……
fulltext_cn: 用AI SLOP对抗克里斯托弗·诺兰是不明智的。
克里斯托弗·诺兰（ Christopher Nolan ）对《奥德赛》（ The Odyssey ）的引人入胜的看法在票房上占据主导地位，并激发了电影观众对经典文学的新兴趣。但是，完全由人工智能制作的故事的新复述是如此糟糕，以至于它可能会让观众完全讨厌原来的故事。

这部名为《奥德修斯：陨落》（ Odysseus: The Fall ）的新电影由人工智能公司Fountain 0制作，由公司联合创始人Ash Koosha编写和导演，他也将自己的肖像借给了主角，并创作了所有的音乐。（这部电影的片尾很短。）该工作室之前唯一的作品是一部名为《紫罗兰之梦》的人工智能电影，该电影于今年早些时候进入翠贝卡。从表面上看，秋天是一个更加雄心勃勃的项目，被称为“第一部完全由人工智能生成的好莱坞大片电影。“实际上，这远不及”好莱坞大片的水平。“这可能并不令人惊讶，但在观看了整个2.5小时的制作之后，我发现自己总是对事情会变得多么糟糕感到惊讶。秋天与瞥见人工智能电影制作的未来相反--它会让你怀疑它是否真的有未来。
这部电影现在可供出租，价格为$ 9.99 ，据我所知，您只能通过网络浏览器观看。为了在客厅电视上观看，我必须用手机镜像屏幕，这并不是70毫米的IMAX。我按下播放键后，情况并没有好转。

堕落受到两个主要问题的困扰。第一是一致性。电影的世界在不断变化，以至于令人难以置信的分心。捕捉奥德修斯和他的人的独眼巨人的高度从一个镜头变成另一个镜头，波浪朝着与风相反的方向移动，嘴巴与说的话不匹配（有时它们根本不发出声音） ，桨随着水手的划船而弯曲和扭曲。在一个场景中，一支庞大的船队正在海洋中驰骋，其中一艘正在莫名其妙地向侧面移动。人工智能制作的画外音可能难以理解，在不同的点上，奥德修斯和宙斯的名字都发错了。
如果只是一个奇怪的打嗝，也许是可以理解的，但The Fall有很多缺点，很难专注于其他任何事情。我和我13岁的孩子一起看了这部电影，它基本上变成了一场寻找最奇怪错误的游戏。我注意到一把剑神奇地变成了一把匕首，然后她发现一具外星人的尸体在吐口水。《The Fall》似乎是一部旨在证明剧本主管存在的原因的电影。

问题是，虽然所有人工智能引发的错误都会分散注意力，但它们也是电影中最有趣的部分。在The Fall中没有太多可以分散注意力的地方，因为它太无聊了。因为目前的人工智能模型实际上只能生成持续几秒钟的场景，所以这部电影感觉就像是一个脱节的奥德赛时刻的集合，这些时刻被小小的押韵或理性缝合在一起。如果你还不知道这个故事，我想你不会知道发生了什么，因为这部电影解释得很少。在电影即将结束之前，你甚至不会了解佩内洛普的追求者。

我也想不出堕落中任何一个方面因为人工智能而感觉有所改善。“表演”令人费解地糟糕，角色在没有明显原因的情况下每次停顿几秒钟，突然爆发出笑声，不知从何而来。行动没有分量，就好像这发生在一个物理和重力等事物是建议而不是常数的世界里。同样，没有这项技术就不可能产生任何酷炫或令人印象深刻的效果。这些怪物看起来像20世纪30年代破旧的停止运动的生物，当它们被放置在人工智能喷出的光滑、超真实的人类角色旁边时，它们就变得更加奇怪了。这不仅令人不安，而且无聊丑陋。

Koosha声称，他之所以改编这个故事，是因为他“自从[他]多年前最初阅读荷马的史诗故事以来，他一直对它充满热情。“看起来更有可能的是，他试图利用诺兰的电影所带来的炒作和能量，将人工智能变成直接到视频的现金抢夺的现代迭代。但这也使这部电影从一开始就处于令人难以置信的劣势，与过去几年最具批判性和商业成功的电影之一进行了比较，由于导演坚持人类工艺，这部电影特别受欢迎。诺兰是一个非常关心电影的人，他的激情和热情正是明星们希望与他合作的原因，观众们纷纷涌向影院观看他的电影。
与此同时， The Fall的存在显示了对媒介的完全蔑视，试图将数百名熟练工人的工作煮沸成一个小团队生产的污水。这太可怕了，会让你更加欣赏人造艺术。

cards.title: Google will now let any AI agent run your smart home
cards.title_cn: 谷歌现在将让任何人工智能代理运行您的智能家居
cards.summary: 【Google】Google is opening up its smart home to AI agents, letting tools like Claude and Open Claw access and control your connected devices and analyze your home's data using the standardized Model Context Pr…
fulltext: ﻿Google Home adds MCP integration, allowing third-party AI agents to analyze your home data, control devices, and build custom dashboards.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Google is opening up its smart home to AI agents, letting tools like Claude and Open Claw access and control your connected devices and analyze your home’s data using the standardized Model Context Protocol.

Google Home MCP is a new integration that lets third-party AI agents control and monitor your smart home and act on your behalf. It “allows any AI agents that support MCP, including Google Antigravity, Claude, Hermes or Open Claw, to securely work with all of the devices and event history in your Google Home ecosystem,” Taylor Lehman, group product manager at Google Home & Nest, said in a blog post.

According to Lehman, Home MCP integration will connect your AI agent of choice to real-world events, enabling a host of new capabilities. From things like cross-camera analysis — so you could ask your agent what your kid did when they got home from school — to using device state history to figure out how many loads of laundry you did last week or how long the lights were left on. It will also allow your agent to interact with you via voice, for example, by sending an audio message over your Google Home speaker when it has finished a task. You can also have your agent create a custom dashboard to control your Google Home.

This doesn’t replace Google’s new Gemini for Home assistant, which remains Google’s interface for interacting with Google Home through the Home app and Google Nest smart speakers, following the demise of Google Assistant. Instead, MCP integration adds another layer of control, allowing third-party AI agents to interact directly with devices connected to Google Home through their own interfaces.
If this week wasn’t dominated by headlines about how AI will kill us all, I’d be really excited about this

At launch, availability is limited to Google Home Premium Advanced users in the US ($20/month or $200/year), with access rolling out in the coming weeks. Setup requires creating a Google Cloud project and configuring it to use the Home MCP.

Giving an AI agent access to real-world devices like smart locks, thermostats, and core infrastructure like HVAC systems and appliances raises obvious questions about security, privacy, and safety. Google says Home MCP enforces rate limits and safety protections; for example, it won’t allow an agent to unlock doors. However, depending on your agent, “connecting it to Home MCP can result in unexpected or even undesired behavior,” said Lehman, who recommends reviewing Google’s developer policies and terms of service.

Home Assistant, an open-source smart home platform, has implemented a similar MCP integration that shows what you can do when you give an agent access to your smart home system. I tested this last year to use Claude to vibe-code my smart home, and it easily handled some of the more complex tasks that most interfaces — and users, for that matter — struggle with, including troubleshooting, creating automations, designing a dashboard, and setting up more advanced configurations, all using natural language.

The biggest change here isn’t that Google Home can now turn your lights on and off through your Claude app; it’s that Claude — or your agent of choice — has access to the underlying data and control layer of your home. It’s a step toward building a whole home computer for your smart home that can understand what’s happening in it, reason across its history, and take action on your behalf. And if this last week wasn’t dominated by headlines about how AI will kill us all, I’d be really excited.
A system that can troubleshoot, suggest improvements, and identify patterns across your home is more useful than one that says “I’m sorry, I can’t do that”

Still, there are real advantages to giving an AI agent access to your smart home. It can reason across the data your home generates and act on it in ways traditional smart home systems generally can’t, moving the smart home from command and control toward something more contextual and proactive, closer to actual intelligence. A system that can troubleshoot a device, suggest improvements to automations, and track and identify patterns across your home is much more useful than one that just says “I’m sorry, I can’t do that.” With Home MCP integration, Google is bringing these capabilities into Google Home.

While consumer-facing tools like Claude will be useful for smart home tinkerers, the bigger picture here is Google’s developer play. Over the last couple of years, Google has increasingly positioned itself as the smart home’s infrastructure layer. It launched API access to its smart home in 2024 and more recently made Gemini for Home a full-stack AI offering. All of this points toward a more B2B2C strategy: Google can provide the AI and smart home infrastructure while other companies build consumer-facing services and products on top.

With this week’s announcement, Google has also opened a path for developers to use its agentic Antigravity coding tool to build custom AI agents for the smart home that tap into Google Home device data and control layer. But even if developers use a different agent, as long as they’re using Google Home, it’s a win for Google. This way, Google becomes the smart home infrastructure layer, in much the same way AWS became infrastructure for internet and software businesses.

Whether smart home developers will buy into Google’s promises here is a big question. Based on the number of smart home platforms the company has launched and let die over the years — Android @ Home, Weave, Project Brillo, Works with Nest, Google Assistant — developers will have to decide whether Google has finally settled on a smart home platform it intends to stick with.

cards.summary_cn: 【Google】谷歌正在向人工智能代理开放其智能家居，让Claude和Open Claw等工具访问和控制您的连接设备，并使用标准化的模型上下文策略分析家中的数据……
fulltext_cn: ﻿ Google Home添加了MCP集成，允许第三方AI代理分析您的家庭数据、控制设备和构建自定义仪表板。
如果您从Verge链接购买东西， Vox Media可能会赚取佣金。查看我们的道德声明。
谷歌正在向人工智能代理开放其智能家居，让Claude和Open Claw等工具访问和控制您的连接设备，并使用标准化的模型上下文协议分析您的家庭数据。
Google Home MCP是一个新的集成，允许第三方AI代理控制和监控您的智能家居并代表您采取行动。Google Home & Nest集团产品经理Taylor Lehman在一篇博客文章中表示： “它允许任何支持MCP的AI代理（包括Google Antigravity、Claude、Hermes或Open Claw ）安全地使用Google Home生态系统中的所有设备和事件历史记录。”

根据雷曼的说法， Home MCP集成将把您选择的人工智能代理与现实世界的事件联系起来，从而实现一系列新功能。从跨摄像头分析（这样您可以询问您的代理您的孩子放学回家后做了什么）到使用设备状态历史记录来计算您上周洗了多少衣服或灯开了多长时间。它还允许您的客服代表通过语音与您互动，例如，在Google Home扬声器完成任务后，通过该扬声器发送语音消息。您也可以让客服代表创建自定义控制面板来控制您的Google Home。
这并不能取代谷歌新推出的Gemini for Home助手，后者仍然是谷歌在Google Assistant消亡后通过Home应用程序和Google Nest智能扬声器与Google Home交互的界面。相反， MCP集成增加了另一层控制，允许第三方AI代理通过自己的界面直接与连接到Google Home的设备进行交互。
如果本周没有关于人工智能将如何杀死我们所有人的头条新闻占据主导地位，我会对此感到非常兴奋
在推出时，仅适用于美国的Google Home Premium高级用户（每月$ 20或每年$ 200 ） ，访问权限将在未来几周内推出。安装程序需要创建Google Cloud项目并将其配置为使用Home MCP。
让人工智能代理访问智能锁、恒温器等真实世界的设备，以及暖通空调系统和电器等核心基础设施，会引发安全、隐私和安全方面的明显问题。Google表示， Home MCP强制执行速率限制和安全保护措施；例如，它不允许客服代表打开门锁。但是，根据您的代理， “将其连接到Home MCP可能会导致意外甚至不希望的行为，”雷曼说，他建议查看Google的开发人员政策和服务条款。
Home Assistant是一个开源的智能家居平台，它实现了类似的MCP集成，展示了当您授予代理访问智能家居系统的权限时，您可以做些什么。去年我用Claude对我的智能家居进行了测试，它可以轻松处理大多数界面和用户难以处理的一些更复杂的任务，包括故障排除、创建自动化、设计仪表板和设置更高级的配置，所有这些都使用自然语言。
这里最大的变化不是Google Home现在可以通过Claude应用打开和关闭灯光，而是Claude （或您选择的代理）可以访问您家的底层数据和控制层。这是朝着为您的智能家居构建一台完整的家用电脑迈出的一步，它可以了解其中发生的事情，推理其历史记录，并代表您采取行动。如果上周没有关于人工智能将如何杀死我们所有人的头条新闻占据主导地位，我会非常兴奋。
一个可以排除故障、提出改进建议并识别整个房源模式的系统比一个说“对不起，我做不到”的系统更有用

尽管如此，让人工智能代理访问您的智能家居还是有真正的优势的。它可以对家庭生成的数据进行推理，并以传统智能家居系统通常无法做到的方式对其进行操作，将智能家居从命令和控制转向更具情境性和主动性、更接近实际智能的东西。一个可以对设备进行故障排除、建议自动化改进以及跟踪和识别整个房源模式的系统，比仅仅说“对不起，我不能这么做。“通过Home MCP集成， Google将这些功能引入Google Home。
虽然像Claude这样的面向消费者的工具对智能家居修补匠来说很有用，但更重要的是谷歌的开发人员。在过去的几年里，谷歌越来越多地将自己定位为智能家居的基础设施层。它于2024年推出了对其智能家居的API访问，最近使Gemini for Home成为全栈AI产品。所有这些都指向了更多的B2B2C战略：谷歌可以提供人工智能和智能家居基础设施，而其他公司则在上面构建面向消费者的服务和产品。
在本周的公告中，谷歌还为开发人员开辟了一条途径，让他们可以使用其代理Antigravity编码工具为智能家居构建自定义AI代理，从而利用Google Home设备数据和控制层。但是，即使开发人员使用不同的代理，只要他们使用Google Home ，这对Google来说也是一场胜利。通过这种方式，谷歌成为智能家居基础设施层，就像AWS成为互联网和软件业务的基础设施一样。
在这里，智能家居开发商是否会接受谷歌的承诺是一个大问题。根据该公司多年来推出的智能家居平台（ Android @ Home、Weave、Project Brillo、Works with Nest、Google Assistant ）的数量，开发人员将不得不决定谷歌是否最终选择了它打算继续使用的智能家居平台。

cards.title: Apple might make servers again to cash in on the AI rush
cards.title_cn: 苹果可能会再次制造服务器，以兑现人工智能热潮
cards.summary: 【Apple】According to The Information, Apple is planning to get back into the server game and might just pair up with Nvidia to make it happen. Apple retired its Xserve line in 2011 and has largely left enterp…
fulltext: The company could borrow tech from Nvidia to make it happen.

According to The Information, Apple is planning to get back into the server game and might just pair up with Nvidia to make it happen. Apple retired its Xserve line in 2011 and has largely left enterprise machines to other manufacturers since. But the growing demand for compute power as the AI industry continues to expand has apparently led the company to believe there is an opening for its powerful but efficient ARM-based M processors. Its Mac Mini and Mac Studio have proven popular with AI developers, which has led to shortages.

The server product, whether it’s called Xserve or something else, likely won’t debut until 2029. Word is that it will run on two or four (depending on the model) M8 Ultra chips. Apple only just announced the M6 in August, so the M8 line is a ways out.

It’s also rumored that Apple’s servers could incorporate Nvidia’s NVLink Fusion tech, which connects multiple chips together so they can operate as one. While the two companies have historically had a frosty relationship behind the scenes, recently Apple turned to Nvidia chips to power its revamped Siri servers. Incorporating NVLink could lead to further collaboration between the two, but plans could still change.

fulltext_cn: 该公司可以借用英伟达的技术来实现这一目标。

据The Information报道，苹果计划重返服务器游戏，并可能与Nvidia合作实现这一目标。苹果公司于2011年退役其Xserve生产线，此后基本上将企业机器留给了其他制造商。但随着人工智能行业的不断扩张，对计算能力的需求不断增长，这显然导致该公司相信其强大而高效的基于ARM的M处理器有一个开放的机会。其Mac Mini和Mac Studio已被证明深受人工智能开发人员的欢迎，这导致了短缺。
服务器产品，无论是名为Xserve还是其他产品，很可能要到2029年才会首次亮相。据说它将在两个或四个（取决于型号） M8 Ultra芯片上运行。苹果刚刚在8月份发布了M6 ，所以M8系列是一个出路。
还有传言称，苹果的服务器可能采用英伟达的NVLink Fusion技术，该技术将多个芯片连接在一起，以便它们可以作为一个芯片运行。虽然两家公司历来在幕后关系冷淡，但最近苹果转向英伟达芯片为其改造后的Siri服务器提供动力。合并NVLink可能会导致两者之间的进一步合作，但计划仍有可能发生变化。

cards.title: Get your subscriptions ready for iOS 27
cards.summary: 【Apple】Discover how you can expand the reach of your subscriptions with new features in iOS 27. You can start preparing today by making sure your apps use StoreKit 2 to handle your Apple In-App Purchases. Re…
fulltext: September 16, 2026
Discover how you can expand the reach of your subscriptions with new features in iOS 27. You can start preparing today by making sure your apps use StoreKit 2 to handle your Apple In-App Purchases.

Offer multiple subscriptions as a single Apple In-App Purchase in your apps with new Bundles and Suites capabilities. With Bundles, people can access multiple subscriptions in one purchase — across a single app, multiple apps from the same developer, or even spanning multiple developers’ apps. With Suites, people get access to a single subscription that seamlessly works across a set of apps from a single developer.
The App Store provides the purchase experience, which displays all apps included in your Bundle or Suite, so it’s easy for people to download and access their subscription content right away.

To get started, review our Bundles and Suites page, which includes eligible configurations, technical requirements, and how to submit a request form. Bundles and Suites will be available later this year in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, tvOS 27, or later.
Offer Bundles and Suites
Bundles and Suites video

Multiseat purchases make it easy for organizations and groups to buy your subscriptions in bulk through Volume Purchasing and Group Purchases. This presents you with an opportunity to expand your subscription beyond single users, as small businesses and specific work groups or departments can access your subscription without having to go through additional administrative workflows.

With Volume Purchasing, organizations that use Apple Business and Apple School Manager can buy your subscriptions through a single Apple In-App Purchase and assign seats using a device management provider.

With Group Purchases, a subscriber can buy multiple seats in a single Apple In-App Purchase and invite others to join. Apple handles any seat assignment and the invitation flow, to let groups — like small businesses, individual departments, or teams — easily access your subscriptions.

This opens your subscription to users who don't fit the traditional single-subscriber model: a work team splitting the cost of a productivity app, a small business outfitting a handful of employees, a department within a larger company, or a group of collaborators sharing access to a creative tool. Any of these groups can become paying subscribers today, without going through IT or procurement.

Starting today, multiseat purchases are enabled by default for subscriptions in App Store Connect. You have full control over availability and can disable multiseat purchases entirely, or selectively manage availability across the App Store, Apple Business, and Apple School Manager.
Volume Purchasing launches on October 22, 2026, and Group Purchases will launch this winter.

Anthropic is merging its front end for Claude chat and Cowork, making it less confusing for people to decide which tab to use for different tasks.

The unified interface lets users access chat, Cowork, and Artifacts (Claude’s interactive workspace feature) within one window. Claude Design, which was introduced in April for website and prototype design, also works anywhere within Claude.

Before this rollout, the company said customers often struggled to choose the right tab for the right task. With the new design, Claude automatically routes requests without having to switch tabs or windows. The idea is to remove confusion about which feature to pick and use just one front end to route work to different parts of the app.
Hopefully, OpenAI also takes a cue from this rollout and fixes ChatGPT’s interface across the platforms.

Anthropic is also adding dedicated features for making presentations and documents. Users can ask the AI assistant to create, edit, and present slides, and it can also download the generated presentation as a PDF or PowerPoint.

Similarly, with the Docs feature, users can work alongside Claude to create sections, ask questions, and comment on completed parts. Users can share generated documents or slides with a link and edit them on their phone.
Users can also ask Claude to start creating a document on desktop, and they can check the progress of the task using the mobile app.
These features are rolling out to Claude’s Pro and Max plans first, on the web, desktop, and mobile over the coming weeks. The company plans to extend them to the free and team tiers later.
The update comes in the wake of an upgrade of Cowork’s memory layer, which helps Claude remember user context across chats.

cards.title: Helping older adults use AI in everyday life
cards.title_cn: 帮助老年人在日常生活中使用人工智能
cards.summary: 【OpenAI】OpenAI and AARP are bringing free, hands-on ChatGPT workshops to 1,000 older adults across 10 U.S. cities to build practical AI skills safely.
fulltext: September 16, 2026
In collaboration with OATS, bringing free, hands-on ChatGPT workshops to 1,000 older adults across 10 U.S. cities

AI should be useful and accessible to everyone. That means making sure people of every age have the support they need to use these tools to help make everyday life easier. For older adults, that can mean getting help planning a trip, understanding a confusing letter or bill, spotting a possible scam, pursuing a new hobby, or staying connected with family and loved ones.

Today, OpenAI Academy, in collaboration with Older Adults Technology Services (OATS) from AARP is hosting the Older Adults AI Skills Jam: a free, in-person learning experience designed to help older adults use ChatGPT confidently and safely. The Jam is part of a multi-year effort OpenAI launched with OATS to help older adults build practical AI skills and stay safe online through its flagship program, Senior Planet.

Data shows that older adults are increasingly using ChatGPT for practical guidance, finding information, and writing. In the U.S., the share of messages associated with people 55+ grew from 6% to nearly 10% in a year.

Online safety is a core part of the program. Part of the workshop includes helping older adults spot scams and use ChatGPT as an additional layer of scrutiny and prevention. It walks through common warning signs, including urgent language, secrecy, and suspicious links, and a simple rule: pause, think, and ask. Tens of millions of times a week, people ask ChatGPT for help evaluating suspicious messages, emails, and websites. This education complements OpenAI’s broader work to prevent, detect, and disrupt fraud and scams.

The Older Adults AI Skills Jam will take place in 10 communities across the country and in partnership with local organizations supporting older adults. We’re proud to collaborate with these organizations and support their communities:
Senior Planet in Denver, Colorado
Senior Planet in Miami, Florida
Senior Planet in San Antonio, Texas
Senior Planet in Montgomery County, Maryland
Senior Planet in Queens, New York
The Mirowitz Center in St. Louis, Missouri
Senior Community Services in Twin Cities, Minnesota
The Nashville Public Library and FiftyForward in Nashville, Tennessee
Fresno EOC in Fresno, California
LEARN Idaho in Boise, Idaho

The AI Skills Jam is part of OpenAI Academy’s broader work to make AI literacy practical and accessible to everyone. It builds on previous events we’ve hosted with nonprofits, small businesses, and K–12 educators.

We are grateful to OATS, our local partners, and the participants joining us across the country. Their questions, ideas, and experiences will help shape future learning resources for older adults to ensure the benefits of this technology reach everyone.

fulltext_cn: 与OATS合作，为美国10个城市的1,000名老年人提供免费的实践ChatGPT研讨会
人工智能应该是有用的，每个人都可以使用。这意味着要确保每个年龄段的人都能获得使用这些工具所需的支持，从而让日常生活更轻松。对于老年人来说，这可能意味着获得规划行程的帮助，理解令人困惑的信件或账单，发现可能的骗局，追求新的爱好，或与家人和亲人保持联系。

今天， OpenAI学院与美国退休人员协会（ AARP ）的老年人技术服务（ OATS ）合作举办了老年人AI技能锦标赛（ Older Adults AI Skills Jam ） ：这是一项免费的面对面学习体验，旨在帮助老年人自信和安全地使用ChatGPT。Jam是OpenAI与OATS推出的多年努力的一部分，旨在通过其旗舰计划Senior Planet帮助老年人建立实用的人工智能技能并保持在线安全。
数据显示，老年人越来越多地使用ChatGPT提供实用指导、查找信息和写作。在美国，与55岁以上人群相关的信息比例在一年内从6%增长到近10%。
在线安全是该计划的核心部分。研讨会的部分内容包括帮助老年人发现诈骗，并使用ChatGPT作为额外的审查和预防层。它会经过常见的警告标志，包括紧急语言、保密和可疑链接，以及一条简单的规则：暂停、思考和询问。人们每周数千万次向ChatGPT寻求帮助，以评估可疑消息、电子邮件和网站。这项教育补充了OpenAI在预防、检测和打击欺诈和诈骗方面的更广泛工作。
